rows.subtype: Approach: allowing feelings and staying with family [Thinking]
rows.description: After the sudden death of a grandfather, a teen lets herself cry, sits with the family through the rituals, and understands that grief is not something to hurry or hide.

rows.subtype: Approach: adjusting study and exam plans with school support [Action]
rows.description: A teen informs the class teacher, asks for extra time on assignments for a few weeks, and rebuilds a lighter schedule, instead of forcing normal performance immediately.

rows.subtype: Approach: suppressing emotion to seem strong [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy told to be the man of the house hides his tears, throws himself into chores and studying, and weeks later finds outbursts and sleeplessness because the grief was never expressed.

rows.subtype: Approach: noticing when grief becomes overwhelming and seeking support [Revision]
rows.description: Months later, a student still cannot concentrate or sleep, so he tells his mother, who arranges a talk with a school counsellor, an appropriate step and not a weakness.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
rows.subtype: Approach: deciding a personal rule for what counts as own work [Thinking]
rows.description: A student decides that AI may explain ideas and check his work, but written answers and graded assignments must be his own, and reads school policy to confirm where the line is.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
rows.subtype: Approach: being open with the teacher about use [Action]
rows.description: A teen tells the teacher she used AI to brainstorm ideas and check grammar, shows her notes, and asks whether this fits the assignment rules, which builds trust and avoids misunderstanding.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
rows.subtype: Approach: copying AI output as homework [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen pastes an AI-written answer to submit, and later cannot explain it in class or solve a similar problem on the test, since the learning never happened.

rows.subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
rows.subtype: Approach: testing understanding without the tool [Revision]
rows.description: After noticing he depends on AI, a student closes it and tries a similar problem cold, sees gaps, and adjusts by asking for hints only after a fair attempt.

rows.subtype: Approach: finding out the topics and format first [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy learns that the inter-school quiz covers general knowledge, science and sports, with buzzer rounds. Knowing the format tells him what to prepare and how quickly he must answer.

rows.subtype: Approach: reading widely from newspapers and books [Action]
rows.description: A girl reads the children's page of the newspaper each day and a general knowledge book at night. She keeps a notebook of new facts about places, people and records.

rows.subtype: Approach: trying to memorise everything in the encyclopedia [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child decides to learn all the facts in a thick book. He soon gets tired and confused, and does not know which facts matter or where he is weak.

rows.subtype: Approach: spotting weak topics and giving them extra time [Revision]
rows.description: After a mock round, the team sees that they miss questions on geography. They spend the next week with a map and an atlas, and their score improves.

rows.subtype: Approach: identify the rule and value at stake [Thinking]
rows.description: Asked by a manager to backdate a document for a client audit, the junior analyst asks what it would mean if the record were false, and recalls company policy and personal integrity. Naming the principle clears the fog of pressure.

rows.subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of the refusal conversation [Thinking]
rows.description: The employee imagines the manager's reactions and prepares calm wording such as offering to fix the delay honestly instead of falsifying records. Rehearsal makes it easier to stay steady under pressure.

rows.subtype: Approach: comply quietly to avoid conflict [Pitfall]
rows.description: Afraid of losing the job, the employee backdates the document and tells no one. The fear of consequences is real, but the person now carries the risk of an audit and the guilt, and may be asked again.

rows.subtype: Approach: escalate to HR or the ethics channel if pressure continues [Revision]
rows.description: When the manager repeats the request, the employee moves from private refusal to a written report to HR or the ethics helpline, keeping details factual. Escalation is used when direct handling does not work.

rows.subtype: Approach: reading the timetable and packing the night before [Action]
rows.description: A boy looks at tomorrow's timetable, takes out yesterday's books and puts in the right notebooks, lunch box and water bottle. Doing it in the evening leaves the morning calm.

rows.subtype: Approach: using a coloured chart pinned on the wall [Action]
rows.description: A girl makes a weekly chart with each subject in a colour and pins it near her study table. Colours help her see at a glance which books belong to which day.

rows.subtype: Approach: throwing everything in the bag just in case [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child keeps all books in the bag so he need not check the timetable. The bag becomes too heavy for his shoulders, and he still cannot find the right notebook in the mess.

rows.subtype: Approach: adding a note about changes to the plan [Revision]
rows.description: After the PT shoe mistake, the girl adds a sticky note to her chart reading Wednesday PT shoes. She also checks the school diary each Sunday for changes to the timetable.

rows.subtype: Approach: matching skills to opportunities [Thinking]
rows.description: A sixteen-year-old lists what he can do, such as fixing phones, drawing or teaching basic Maths, and then checks which are legal and safe for his age and can fit around school.

rows.subtype: Approach: minimum viable version of a small business [Action]
rows.description: The student starts by making ten handmade greeting cards for festival season, sells them to relatives and neighbours, and uses the response to decide whether to make more.

rows.subtype: Approach: taking any offer without thinking [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student accepts a night delivery job with vague terms from a stranger. It looks like easy money, but it is unsafe, may be illegal for a minor and clashes with school hours.

rows.subtype: Approach: buffer and weekly hour cap [Revision]
rows.description: After a dip in marks, the student caps work to six hours a week and blocks exam months completely, agreeing with parents on when to pause the gig.
